mainEntity.name: Should I use AI automation or regular no-code automation for repetitive tasks?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Standard automation is often better for fixed rules, while AI is more useful when the workflow must interpret varied text, summarize research, classify information, or draft language. Many practical systems combine both: conventional triggers and integrations around an AI step.

## Context
Run My AI Business examples include recurring research, content drafting, prospect preparation, billing checks, and support workflows. Some steps are predictable and should not be made more complex merely because AI is available.

## Key factors
- Consistency of the input
- Need for interpretation or language generation
- Consequence of a wrong result
- Availability of reliable rules and structured data

## Practical guidance
Label every step as rule-based, AI-assisted, or human-only before building. Use the simplest method that meets the requirement, then add AI where ambiguity or unstructured information creates real value.

This avoids turning straightforward tasks into fragile systems.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use regular automation for fixed, predictable rules and AI where the workflow must interpret text, summarize information, classify records, or draft language. Combining both is often best: reliable triggers and integrations surrounding a limited AI step.
